You can call me a half-vegetation and half-(meta)community ecologist.

I am a latina from **Brazil**, so if you like we can talk in *Portuguese*!
I consider myself fluent in English (but I am always trying to improve) and a beginner*ish* in French (we can give it a try!).

I got my **BSc in Biology** (2021) and **MSc in EcoEvoBio** (2024) from Universidade Estadual Paulista (UNESP), in Rio Claro, Brazil. Where I also worked as research technian for a year (2025) with data management of the [Cerrado On Fire](https://bv.fapesp.br/pt/bolsas/224767/implementacao-de-um-banco-de-dados-sobre-dados-ecologicos-de-comunidades-de-plantas-sob-manejo-de-fo/)

I started working on disturbance ecology during my BSc, when I first studied changes in beta diversity in communities under different fire regimes. 
Later, I investigated the combined effects of biological invasion and fire on communities.
My interest in vegetation ecology grew through the years, as I have always been working with the herbaceous-shrub layer of the Cerrado (the most beautiful biome in the world). But last year I started having different questions - which lead me more to questions related to how **disturbance** shapes **biodiversity**.

In my current research, I investigate how novel disturbance regimes affect different components of biodiversity in an integrated framework that considers different temporal, spatial, and organizational scales. Although my work is often focused on fire-driven ecosystems, I am also open to working with and discussing other types of disturbances, such as **droughts and herbivory**, and in how these processes shape **open ecosystems** and plant communities in general.

I’m really into **open science, good data practices**, and all the conversations around making **research better and more accessible**. I could happily spend a long time talking about FAIR principles and related topics. These interests have also led me to think more broadly about the *kind of academic culture we build*, which is why I’ve been spending more of my recent time engaging with questions around equity and mental well-being in academia.

If you are interested in discussing or collaborating on any of these topics, feel free to get in touch.
